_comment: Golden vectors for fractional indexing (F5.5). Hand-computed from the
order-key scheme described in server/src/domain/position.ts, not generated
by it (F4). Both the TypeScript and the Kotlin implementations must
reproduce every `expected` exactly, or the two clients will disagree about
list order and neither build will notice.
The digit alphabet is base-62 in ASCII order:
0-9, then A-Z, then a-z. Index 31 is 'V', index 16 is 'G'.

between.why: First item in an empty list. 'a' means an integer part of length 2.
Append: increment the integer part. No fractional part is needed.
Append across the 62-item boundary: 'az' rolls over into a longer integer part.
Prepend: decrement below 'a0' into the negative half of the encoding.
Prepend again, still within the same integer length.
Insert between adjacent integers: midpoint of digit 0 and 62 is index 31, 'V'.
Insert again on the low side: midpoint of 0 and 31 is 15.5, rounded to 16, 'G'.
Insert on the high side of the same pair: midpoint of 31 and 62 is 46.5, rounded to 47, 'l'.
A gap wider than one digit needs only one character, however long the neighbours are.

ordering.why: Sorted ascending by plain byte comparison. A locale-aware comparator would reorder these, which is why the client must not use one.

invalid.why: Every one of these must be rejected rather than stored.
